summary: Discovery call focused on data residency and compliance requirements for deploying Redwood. Great Lakes Financial (GLF) needs clarity on whether Hosted can meet their EU/US data residency, GLBA/PCI/SOC2 controls, and log retention restrictions. They are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) with constraints around encryption keys (customer-managed KMS), limited logs for regulator audits, and vendor access. Next steps: send security docs, run cost/latency comparison, and schedule technical deep dive for VPC/KMS testing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-14 15:00 EDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Li (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Daniel Rivera (CTO, GLF), Aisha Khan (Head of Security), Tom Brooks (Compliance)

Summary: Quick intro, then deep dive into GLF compliance needs, followed by technical constraints around KMS and log retention. Action items reviewed at the end.

[00:00] Marcus: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Marcus from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with Priya who is our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Daniel: good thanks, uh we wanted to make sure this is mostly a compliance/data residency discovery — we've got a lot of questions on whether we can use hosted or we need dedicated or private.
[00:20] Marcus: perfect, that's what we wanted to cover. quick sanity check — who's driving this on your side? is it compliance or platform?
[00:27] Aisha: hi i'm Aisha, head of security so i'm leading requirements and coordinating with Tom on compliance. Daniel is overall sponsor.
[00:35] Tom: yeah i'm compliance, focused on GLBA and PCI implications for any vendor handling customer financial data.
[00:42] Priya: great, thanks. i'll try to cover the technical constraints. first, can you describe the data types that will hit Redwood? pii, account numbers, transaction history, anything health-related?
[00:54] Daniel: mostly transaction summaries, account metadata, and some KYC fields; no PHI but we do have some cross-border accounts for EU customers, so GDPR applies.
[01:05] Priya: okay makes sense. so main concerns are residency for EU subjects, auditability, and encryption key control.
[01:12] Marcus: to frame the options — Hosted is our managed API with multi-region model catalog; Dedicated is reserved capacity for you in a region with stronger isolation; Private is with a customer-managed VPC or on-prem install. cost and operational overhead move up as isolation increases.
[01:29] Aisha: can you confirm if Hosted ever stores customer data in non-request logs? specifically we have a regulator requirement that certain PII must not leave EU or must be logged and retained only in specific ways.
[01:41] Marcus: good question. by default we retain request logs for troubleshooting and billing, but we have configurable retention policies and an option for log redaction and minimization for enterprise plans. we can also route EU traffic to EU regions.
[01:53] Tom: do you offer customer-managed keys? regulator says vendor shouldn't have decryption access to certain fields.
[01:58] Priya: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS (HSM-backed) and you can configure envelope encryption so that sensitive blobs are encrypted with your key. Hosted can support bring-your-own-key for some enterprise customers but there are caveats around key ops. sometimes the managed host still needs read access for payload processing — we can go into details in the tech deep dive.
[02:22] Daniel: what about logs — auditors often require detailed request logs for a 7-year window, but our security team wants to avoid storing full request bodies. is there a way to keep metadata only?
[02:33] Marcus: yes, we can set log retention windows and choose to store metadata only. for some controls we do produce audit logs for admin actions (SSO, role changes) and request-level telemetry can be redacted or hashed. note that for model debugging we sometimes need more context; this is a tradeoff.
[02:49] Aisha: also need SOC2 and ISO certifications, and any red teams or pen test reports you have.
[02:55] Marcus: we'll share SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 and our latest penetration test summary.
[03:01] Priya: practical question on connectivity — do you require a public internet egress or can we establish VPC peering / PrivateLink?
[03:09] Daniel: we prefer private connectivity.
[03:11] Priya: Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Redwood Private is deployed inside your VPC or on-prem. for Hosted we can provide region-restricted endpoints but typically it's over the public internet unless you sign an enterprise network arrangement.
[03:26] Tom: timeline wise, we have an RFP for vendors by end of next month. we need to know if Hosted is acceptable or if we must require Dedicated/Private. what is the typical go-live time for Dedicated vs Private?
[03:38] Marcus: Dedicated provisioning can be weeks depending on capacity and contract; Private on-prem is months because of packaging and network integration. Hosted is immediate.
[03:46] Daniel: cost differential?
[03:48] Marcus: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract (monthly/annual commit) — cheaper unit cost but higher commit. Private has setup fee plus ongoing support. Priya can sketch out a rough estimate for a 16k token sequence workload during the follow-up.
[03:59] Priya: yes i'll produce a side-by-side: latency and cost for streaming generation with 8–16k seq, with and without KV cache, and show quantization suggestions to reduce GPU cost.
[04:12] Aisha: about log residency — some EU regulators require logs to remain in EU and not be accessible by non-EU employees. can you restrict admin access by geography?
[04:23] Priya: we have role-based access controls (RBAC) and admin actions are logged; for Dedicated and Private you can enforce SSO, IP restrictions, and keep control plane or key management under your control. for Hosted we have contractual isolation and can also offer access restrictions for enterprise customers.
[04:41] Tom: are you PCI scoped? we may route card processing metadata to other systems, but anything that touches PAN is tightly controlled.
[04:49] Marcus: Redwood isn't a payment processor; we recommend tokenizing or removing PAN before sending. we can help with best practices and support field redaction in the client SDK.
[04:58] Daniel: curious about fallback behavior — if Dedicated goes down do you have automatic fallback to Hosted models?
[05:04] Priya: yes we offer smart routing and fallback policies; you can configure failover to compatible model variants in a different region or to Hosted with a different SLA. for strict compliance you'd likely keep traffic in a region but you can have a read-only fallback.
[05:18] Aisha: we also need an explanation of how you handle GDPR data subject requests and right-to-be-forgotten — do you have deletion APIs for request logs?
[05:28] Marcus: yes we have APIs to purge logs and data associated with a customer on request; for Hosted we maintain documented retention and deletion processes, for Dedicated/Private you can manage retention yourself.
[05:40] Tom: on auditability, our auditors want immutable audit logs for admin actions and key rotation history. can you export those logs to our SIEM?
[05:50] Priya: we support log streaming to customer endpoints (S3, Event Hubs, Kafka) for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can push to customer-managed sinks under enterprise agreements.
[06:03] Daniel: any regional limitations for model catalog? like are some open models not available in certain regions?
[06:09] Marcus: most models in our catalog are replicated to major regions; there are some licensing constraints on certain third-party models but we can provide a compatibility matrix.
[06:20] Aisha: ok, let's talk about KMS — if we use customer-managed KMS, what's the key lifecycle? do you perform key wrapping or do you ever hold plaintext?
[06:30] Priya: we use envelope encryption. the customer key (in their cloud KMS or HSM) encrypts a data key, the runtime uses the data key to encrypt payloads. Redwood doesn't store plaintext for fields you mark as sensitive. for Hosted there's a managed arranger where keys might be in a Redwood-managed HSM; for Dedicated/Private keys stay in the customer domain. we'll bring the cryptographic flow diagram.
[06:54] Marcus: i'll note that for some features like model tuning or caching we may need ephemeral access to nonce-level KV cache; we can discuss methods to minimize retained sensitive contexts.
[07:06] Tom: we have a hard requirement: auditors want ability to verify that no EU customer PII was processed in a US region. is it feasible to lock a model to an EU-only deployment?
[07:17] Priya: yes, you can pin traffic to EU-only variants and restrict routing. for Dedicated you can provision capacity only in EU regions. Hosted can be configured to route EU traffic to EU endpoints under an enterprise tenancy.
[07:32] Daniel: are there customers in financial services using your Private deployment?
[07:36] Marcus: yes we have several banks using Dedicated and a few large institutions using our Private on-prem package for regulated workloads. happy to share references under NDA.
[07:45] Aisha: what about data residency for backups and snapshots — are they encrypted and region-located?
[07:51] Priya: backups are encrypted at rest and located in the same region by default; for Dedicated/Private you can control snapshot policy and location.
[07:59] Marcus: i'd like to understand success criteria — what does GLF need to see to pick Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
[08:06] Daniel: checklist: 1) explicit EU-only residency for EU data, 2) customer-managed KMS for certain fields, 3) log redaction options, 4) exportable immutable audit logs, 5) pen test / SOC2 evidence, 6) cost within our budget.
[08:20] Priya: great that's helpful. we'll map features to those criteria when we send follow-up docs.
[08:26] Tom: about cost, if we go Dedicated what kind of commitment are we talking about?
[08:31] Marcus: typical Dedicated contracts are monthly or annual capacity commitments; discounts depend on term length. Priya will run sample numbers.
[08:40] Aisha: need to confirm whether Redwood staff can access production logs for debugging; regulator may require no access without a legal process.
[08:49] Priya: we can limit access and require an approval workflow for any production access; for Dedicated/Private you can keep those controls within your environment.
[08:59] Daniel: any special requirements for PII in transit — do you support mutual TLS?
[09:05] Priya: yes we support mTLS for private endpoints and mutual auth for some enterprise arrangements.
[09:12] Marcus: at this point i want to propose concrete next steps: we'll send our security package and a draft SOW for Dedicated/Private options; Priya will prepare an engineering note with the KMS flow and latency/cost estimates; and we'll schedule the SE-led technical deep dive for next week. sound ok?
[09:29] Daniel: yes.
[09:31] Aisha: yes.
[09:33] Tom: yes.
[09:35] Priya: quick question — do you have any strict restrictions on logs retention length?
[09:40] Aisha: for EU PII we need a specified retention TTL, and for certain logs we must keep them for audit purposes for 7 years — but we can hash or pseudonymize request bodies.
[09:51] Priya: got it, we'll outline options: full retention to your S3, metadata-only storage, or hashed pseudonymized bodies.
[09:59] Marcus: closing the loop, we'll also share references in financial services and a sample contract clause for data residency.
[10:05] Daniel: one more thing — are there any limitations on model caching that could inadvertently store PII?
[10:12] Priya: we have KV cache features; caching is configurable and can be disabled for sensitive routes. where caching is enabled you can set TTL and automatic redaction.
[10:25] Tom: can you provide a minimal data flow diagram showing where data lives, where keys are held, and where logs flow? auditors will want that.
[10:33] Marcus: yes, will include with the security pack.
[10:37] Aisha: timeline question — if we do a small pilot on Hosted with strict retention and EU routing, is that sufficient to meet the RFP?
[10:46] Tom: possibly, but auditors are cautious — they may want Dedicated if they can't see technical proof.
[10:53] Priya: we can propose a pilot: Hosted with EU-only routing, data redaction, and customer-managed KMS for the critical fields. run a 4-week pilot and then evaluate.
[11:06] Daniel: sounds reasonable.
[11:09] Marcus: ok great. we'll follow up with docs and schedule the deep dive. thanks everyone.
